001_N: ["You tap your card for a coffee. Five dollars.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
002_N: ["Beep. And the number above your head drops by five.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
003_N: ["Not five dollars. Five minutes. Of your life.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
004_N: ["What if every dollar you spent cost you one minute of your life?",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
008_N: ["And one day, you'll get a bill that isn't even yours.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
009_N: ["Let's go back to that morning. One hour before the coffee.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
010_N: ["You wake up, shuffle to the mirror, and there it is. A glowing number over your head.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
012_N: ["Your best friend Marco sees it too. Marco once microwaved a fork just to see what happens. So naturally, he wants to experiment on you.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
013_N: ["He grabs a pack of gum and makes you pay. One dollar.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
015_N: ["Rule number one: every dollar you pay costs one minute of your life.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
016_N: ["You do the math. Twenty-seven million minutes. Technically, you're a multi-millionaire. Just not in dollars.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
017_N: ["Then Marco buys you a burger. Twelve dollars.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
019_N: ["Rule number two: if someone else pays, it's free.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
020_N: ["On Friday, your paycheck lands. Two thousand dollars.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
021_N: ["You check the number at lunch. At dinner. At three in the morning. It doesn't go up. Not by a single minute.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
022_N: ["Rule number three: earning money never gives time back. Only spending takes it.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
023_N: ["So your life is a bank account. You can only withdraw. Never deposit.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
024_N: ["Then came the coffee. And the rent. You know that part.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
026_N: ["A streaming subscription, sixteen dollars a month. Sixteen minutes, every month, for a show you fall asleep to.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
028_N: ["Groceries, eighty-four dollars. An hour and twenty-four minutes. You put back the fancy cheese. Then you put back the normal cheese.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
029_N: ["A taxi across town, thirty dollars. Thirty minutes. Walking takes forty.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
030_N: ["So you walk, feeling smart. Until you realize you just spent forty minutes to save thirty.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
031_N: ["A new phone, one thousand dollars. Almost seventeen hours.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
032_N: ["A gym membership you never use, forty dollars a month. You've been paying minutes just to feel guilty.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
033_N: ["Your friend's wedding in Miami. Flight, hotel, gift. Two thousand dollars. Almost a day and a half of your life. You send a card.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
034_N: ["The average new car in America costs about forty-eight thousand dollars. That's thirty-three days of your life. For a car.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
035_N: ["And rent is the real monster. Fifteen hundred a month is twelve and a half days of your life, every single year.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
036_N: ["Benjamin Franklin wrote, remember that time is money, back in seventeen forty-eight. He meant it as advice. For you, it's a receipt.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
037_N: ["But you get good at this. Really good.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
038_N: ["Coupons. Free samples. Birthday parties with free cake. You haven't paid for lunch in two weeks.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
040_N: ["But there's a catch nobody warns you about.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
041_N: ["Rule two says it's free if someone else pays. So you let them.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
042_N: ["Marco pays for dinner. Then the movies. Then the gas.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
043_N: ["On a date, the check arrives, and you study the ceiling for a very long time.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
044_N: ["Mom calls and asks why you never visit. A visit means a bus ticket. A bus ticket means minutes. So you say you're busy.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
045_N: ["Slowly, people notice. You're the guy who never pays.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
047_N: ["Your birthday comes, and nobody plans anything. Planning means somebody pays, and everyone knows who won't.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
048_N: ["And it hits you. You're saving minutes, but you're losing people.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
050_N: ["In twenty seventeen, Harvard researcher Ashley Whillans and her team surveyed more than six thousand people in four countries.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
051_N: ["The people who paid to save time, like paying someone to do the chores they hate, were more satisfied with their lives.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
052_N: ["In another experiment, people got forty dollars on two different weekends. Once they spent it on stuff. Once on something that saved them time. The time purchase made them feel better.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
053_N: ["Researchers even have a name for always feeling short on time. Time poverty. And money can fix it, if you spend it right.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
054_N: ["Money that buys you time is the best money you'll ever spend. Money that costs you people is the worst.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
055_N: ["If this video made you count your minutes, hit subscribe. It costs you nothing. Literally.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
056_N: ["And then, one night, the envelope slides under your door.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
058_N: ["Her surgery. Ninety thousand dollars the insurance won't cover. Due Friday.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
059_N: ["Ninety thousand minutes. That's sixty-two days of your life.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
060_N: ["You know the trick. Rule two. Start a fundraiser, let strangers pay, lose nothing.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
061_N: ["But fundraisers take weeks. Mom has four days.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
062_N: ["You sit on the kitchen floor with the envelope and run the numbers again and again. They don't change.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
063_N: ["You call Marco. You haven't talked in a month. He picks up on the first ring.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
064_N: ["He says just one thing. Go. I'm coming with you.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
065_N: ["You take the first bus to the hospital. Four dollars. You don't even look up.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
066_N: ["Mom is sitting in a plastic chair, holding the same envelope. She tries to smile. She says, we'll figure it out, honey.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
067_N: ["At the front desk, you open the payment screen. Ninety thousand. Pay.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
069_N: ["The number rolls down. Two months, gone in a second.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
070_N: ["And all you feel is relief. Two months of your life, for years of hers.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
071_N: ["Marco puts a hand on your shoulder. Two months, he says. Let's make sure the rest are good ones.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
072_N: ["Mom sees the number over your head for the first time. She doesn't understand it. But she understands your face.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
074_N: ["In real life, the federal minimum wage in America is seven dollars and twenty-five cents an hour.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
075_N: ["That means for millions of people, one dollar already costs about eight minutes of work.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
076_N: ["Your curse wasn't a curse. It was a discount.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
077_N: ["We all pay in minutes. You were just the only one who could see the price.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
078_N: ["Every shift, every overtime hour, every late night at the office. That's minutes, turned into dollars, turned into stuff.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
079_N: ["A week later, Mom is home. Marco comes over. You buy him a coffee.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
082_N: ["Because the real question was never how much something costs. It's how much of your life it's worth.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
083_N: ["So tell me. If you could see the price of everything in minutes of your life, what would you stop buying first?",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
